a: Atomic radius, ionization energy, and electronegativity show periodic trends.
Electronegativity is the tendency to attract electrons in a bond.
Ionization energy is energy to remove an electron from an atom.
Valence electrons are the outermost electrons involved in bonding.
Lewis structures show valence electrons as dots and bonds.
VSEPR predicts molecular shapes from electron pair repulsion.
Hybridization models mixing of atomic orbitals for bonding.
Balance redox by atoms and charge, often via half-reactions.
K relates equilibrium concentrations/pressures of products and reactants.
